GM Recalls Chevy Express and GMC Savana Vans for Potential Steering Gear Assembly Issue
9 photos
Photo: GMC
As fate would have it, General Motors now has to fix a problem it thought it had already remedied. The largest manufacturer among Detroit's Big Three is aware of certain vans fitted with steering gear assemblies that may contain a loose nut. General Motors already recalled these vans under campaign 26V399 earlier this year, but alas, the previous recall missed a bunch of suspect gear assemblies.
The root cause behind the second recall, which is referred to as 26V718 by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, is the supplier. A malfunctioning part sensor at Nexteer Automotive's facility allowed some assemblies to pass inspection without the subject nut being properly torqued.
GM launched the first campaign, which covered 51 suspect steering gear assembly serial numbers, in June 2026. Dealers were instructed to inspect all vehicles against the provided list of serial numbers, replace matching assemblies, and close non-matching vans after inspection.
A General Motors quality manager then filed a report in September 2026 after a dealer found a loose nut in a 2025 model year Chevrolet Express, namely a vehicle that had already been inspected and closed under the prior campaign. The subsequent investigation matched the serial number to the disposition list, with GM and Nexteer determining that up to 108 serial numbers had been incorrectly omitted. How come?
General Motors believed all those suspect parts were still contained by Nexteer. Affected vehicle identification numbers are now searchable on the NHTSA 's portal, Chevy's website, and GMC's website for Savana owners. GM has instructed Chevrolet and GMC dealers to inspect serial numbers against the expanded list and, if there's a match, replace the steering gear assembly at no charge to affected customers.
Photo: GMC Nexteer's replacement steering gears have nuts torqued to specification. The condition was apparently contained at the supplier back in May 2026, and vans built after June 1, 2026, feature properly fastened nuts. For extra peace of mind, GM also updated the service bulletin for 26V399 to add the missing serial numbers.
GM says that notification letters are scheduled to be mailed on December 14, 2026. Until then, the easiest way to tell if your van is potentially affected is to use the aforementioned VIN lookup tools.
The second recall covers 2025 and 2026 models, with production dates ranging from January 21, 2025, through June 1, 2026. Both full-size vans are primarily made at Wentzville Assembly in Missouri. Cutaway van chassis variants, meanwhile, hail from the International Motors plant in Springfield, Ohio.
Wentzville is the perfect place for the full-size vans because it's optimized for such vehicles and body-on-frame designs. In addition, Wentzville also makes the Colorado and Canyon mid-size trucks. For the base-chassis variants, which are meant for conversions like ambulances and box trucks, International Motors is the right partner, as it is specialized in commercial vehicles and medium-duty trucks.
